transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. New York Democratic Governor Kathy
Hochul says the woman who accused members of a Cornell University fraternity of gang
rape was failed by people obligated to protect her, including police and the county prosecutor.
In what world would the police learn from a victim that she'd been literally gang raped
while intoxicated by five men in a fraternity house and not elevate those allegations to
the district attorney? In what world is the district attorney not even interview her or
anyone else involved or even request the full transcript?
Hochul appointed State Attorney General Letitia James to take over the case as special prosecutor.
The governor says she made the decision after learning that the district attorney closed
the case without having anyone interview the victim or anyone involved in the alleged attack.
She also criticized the Cornell University Police Department for not fully conveying the
woman's story to prosecutors. G7 world leaders say they will coordinate the release of 100
million barrels of crude oil over the next four months, including a substantial release
of diesel fuel within the first 20 days in an effort to stabilize prices. NPR's Elinor
Beardsley reports French President Emmanuel Macron called the G7 meeting after pressure
from President Trump. President Trump had threatened to stop exports of U.S. diesel entirely in
an attempt to lower U.S. prices ahead of the midterm elections. French President Emmanuel
Macron has previously said such a move would be a catastrophe. European governments are
also under huge pressure from their populations as the price of gas and diesel skyrockets.
The G7 leaders said they agreed on the coordinated measures that would help stabilize energy
supplies, shield households and businesses from price shocks, and strengthen the long-term
resilience of global energy systems.
Elinor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris. Democrats are expanding the map of congressional races
they say could be winnable in this fall's midterms. As NPR's Tamara Keith reports,
the new list includes 66 districts. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is pushing
into traditionally Republican territory, adding districts in Kansas, North Carolina, Texas
and Oklahoma, among others, to its districts in playlist. That is a list of congressional
districts where the party committee thinks it can be competitive. It doesn't mean the
Democratic candidates in these races have an easy path to victory, but it does mean
Democrats are bullish about their chances overall. Republicans are projecting confidence
as well, with Speaker Mike Johnson traveling around the country, saying he thinks his party
will expand its House majority. Tamara Keith, NPR News.
U.S. employers added a lackluster 29,000 jobs, and the unemployment rate ticked up last month.
Next month, voters go to the polls in pivotal midterm elections at a time of discontent
over the high cost of living and state of the economy. U.S. stocks rose today. You are
listening to NPR News from Washington.
A Venezuelan delivery driver who was shot by a federal immigration agent in Texas has
had surgery to remove the bullet lodged in his back. A spokesperson for the legal team
of 28-year-old Wilbur Rafael Garces Perez says the surgery was yesterday. Authorities say
that nearly two weeks ago the agent shot Garces Perez after he struck the agent with the side
mirror of a vehicle while trying to evade arrest. Authorities in the Democratic Republic
of Congo say that more than 4,000 people have died of Ebola. Michael Kolokie reports the
government is facing serious challenges to its Ebola response system.
The latest Ebola death toll figures come in the wake of several strikes by health workers
in the country. Earlier this week, the workers held a protest in Ituri province, the epicenter
of the outbreak, over what they called delayed wage payments. Meanwhile, the United Nations
has accused members of the country's military of recently burning down a transit center
for Ebola patients in the east of the country, as soldiers carried out a search for weapons
in the area. And the World Health Organization has raised concern about the Ebola virus spreading
rapidly into new health zones in Congo, stretching already limited resources. For NPR News, I'm
Michael Kolokie in Nairobi.
Experts say the Nobel Peace Prize might go to the International Space Station this year,
highlighting global cooperation. But terrestrial contenders include President Trump, Canadian
Prime Minister Mark Carney, and emergency teams in Sudan. The Norwegian Nobel Committee
will announce the winner on October 9th. The prize often focuses on the durability of peace
and international fraternity. This is NPR.
